_comment: Mutation testing for the competitor-corpus checker. This script is a gate: it blocks commits, and it regenerates three documents that 90 captures link into. A silently-passing test here does not fail loudly — it lets the gate rot while continuing to report success, which is the exact failure mode mutation testing exists to catch. Scoped to the one file, matching the @hobo/core config's stance that a gate nobody runs is not a gate.
_sandbox: Stryker copies the repo into a sandbox per run. Two constraints shape this list. Unbounded, it walks examples/wasp-opensaas/app and dies on a symlinked skills directory (EISDIR on copyfile). But examples/ cannot be excluded wholesale either: docs/competitors/wasp.md links into examples/wasp-opensaas/HOBO.md, and the suite's real-corpus test would then fail the dry run on a broken link that exists only inside the sandbox. So the exclusion is exactly the symlinked subtree. packages/ and external/ are excluded because nothing under mutation reads them and copying them costs far more than it returns.
_baseline: Measured 2026-08-20 on first run: 69.45% overall (432 killed, 148 survived, 42 with no coverage), 47 seconds. break is set at 60 to hold the line already achieved rather than fail from day one; raise it as the score improves. The 42 no-coverage mutants are almost entirely the CLI entry point (`invokedDirectly` and the process.exit path), which unit tests deliberately do not drive.
